newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds closed higher on Thursday with little news but U.S. data supported the market and dealers squared positions ahead of long week end.
"Without any bad news the market is still optimistic," a dealer in Madrid said, explaining that this morning there were fears of other negative remarks about EMU.
"But nothing happened and so the prices recovered from their previous losses," he explained.
Higher-than-expected weekly U.S. jobless claims boosted the U.S. market, giving support to Euro bonds as well. But market is focusing on Friday data about October U.S. unemployment.
Forecasters had put the possible increase in the U.S. payrolls around 212,000. "If anything, the U.S. market has more downside than upside," a dealer here in Madrid said.
On Friday Spanish market will be closed for a holiday.
The 10-year spread over German Bunds slimmed to 179 basis points from 182 this morning while the differential with Italian Btps widened to 35 bp from 31 bp.
The three-year bechmark 7.80 percent closed at 102.76 from 102.53 at yesterday's close.
